overview.title: A Night in the Dunes
overview.p1: A desert camp is the classic way to experience the Sahara: arrive by camel at sunset, settle into a Berber tent among the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi and spend the night under a sky full of stars.
overview.p2: Evenings usually include mint tea, a traditional tagine dinner and drumming around the fire, followed by a sunrise walk up the dunes. Comfort ranges from simple bivouacs to luxury tents, so confirm what is included when you book.
overview.p3: Pair your night at camp with a camel trek, a visit to Khamlia or the fossil workshops to make the most of your time in Merzouga.

1.title: Sunset Arrival
1.desc: Reach camp by camel or 4x4 as the dunes turn golden.

2.title: Dinner & Music
2.desc: Tagine, mint tea and drumming around the fire.

3.title: Stars & Sunrise
3.desc: Total silence, a sky full of stars and a sunrise walk on the dunes.

food.title: Dining at the Camp
food.p1: Meals are usually included in your stay and served in a communal tent or under the stars.
food.li2: Traditional tagine cooked for the group
food.li4: Sunrise breakfast with bread, jam and fresh juice
food.li5: Dates and tea around the campfire
food.p2: Book half-board with your camp; there are no restaurants out in the dunes after dark.

tips.title: Practical Tips for a Desert Camp Stay

1.title: Pack Light
1.desc: Bring a small overnight bag; larger luggage is often left at the hotel or carried separately.

2.title: Trusted Operators
2.desc: Book licensed camps and check what is included: transport, dinner, breakfast and bedding.

3.title: Cold Nights
3.desc: Desert temperatures drop sharply after sunset — bring a warm layer, especially in winter.

q1.question: How long do I need at a desert camp?
q1.answer: Most visitors stay one night: arrive around sunset and leave after sunrise. Two nights allow a slower pace.

q2.question: Is there an entrance fee for the camp?
q2.answer: The dunes are free to access, but a camp stay is a paid package, usually including a camel ride, dinner and breakfast.

q3.question: When is the best time to stay at a desert camp?
q3.answer: Spring and autumn offer comfortable temperatures; summer days are very hot and winter nights are cold.

q4.question: How do I get to the camp?
q4.answer: Most camps are reached by camel trek or 4x4 from Merzouga village; your host usually arranges the transfer.

q5.question: What should I bring?
q5.answer: A light overnight bag, a warm layer, sunglasses, a scarf, sunscreen, a flashlight and some small cash for tips.
